@@U02232@@
You are gathered here together under an auspicious star that promises prosperity and happiness. But why, I ask you, why at just this time, when we would free ourselves of cares and troubles, when we long to pull on mummers’ masks for Carnival and do nothing so much as enjoy ourselves— why, then, are we met, why do we torment ourselves with affairs of state? But since you said it had to be, well, then, let it be!

@@U02234@@
Justice, that highest of virtues, rests on the Emperor's head like a halo. He alone has the power to exercise it. What all men love, demand, desire, what they desperately need, it is his prerogative to give them, his subjects, his people. Ah, but what good is intelligence to the mind, goodness to the heart, readiness to the hand, when the body politic rages with fever, and one single evil spawns a whole host of evils? One glance from this height across your vast empire, Sire, will reveal a nightmare in which Deformity reigns among deformities, where Lawlessness rules in place of law, and Error multiplies and populates the earth. One man steals cattle, another a neighbor's wife, and a third runs off with the altar’s chalice, candlestick, and crucifix, and they end up boasting about it for years without a scratch to limb or reputation.
translation:
@@U02232@@
你们聚集在一颗预示着繁荣和幸福的吉祥星下。但我问你，为什么在这个时候，当我们要摆脱忧虑和烦恼的时候，当我们渴望戴上小丑面具参加狂欢节，除了享受自己之外什么也不做的时候——那么，为什么我们会相遇，为什么我们要用国家事务来折磨自己呢？不过既然你都这么说了，那好吧，那就这样吧！

@@U02234@@
正义是最高的美德，它像光环一样戴在皇帝的头上。只有他有权力行使它。所有人所喜爱、要求、渴望的东西，以及他们迫切需要的东西，他有特权给予他们、他的臣民、他的人民。啊，但是，当政治体因发烧而肆虐，而一种邪恶会滋生出一大堆邪恶时，聪明对于头脑、善良对于心灵、准备就绪又有什么好处呢？陛下，从这个高度看一眼您广阔的帝国，就会发现一场噩梦，其中畸形统治着畸形，无法无天取代了法律，错误在地球上繁殖和蔓延。一个人偷了牛，另一个人偷了邻居的妻子，还有一个人偷走了祭坛上的圣杯、烛台和十字架，最后他们吹嘘了很多年，没有伤到四肢，也没有名声大噪。
